clips.title: The story
paras: In Silverpine Forest, Until Death Do Us Part brings Clarice Foster’s old grief to Yuriv’s grave. From the Pools of Vision beneath Thunder Bluff, the Forsaken asks you to leave her keepsake pendant on the tomb of the husband who abandoned her and their children.

Clarice Foster remembers her mortal marriage without fondness. As Lordaeron crumbled, Yuriv left her and their children to join a crusade against the rising undead, declaring service to the Holy Light paramount. His devotion saved neither his family nor himself. Clarice was raised into undeath, while Yuriv lies beneath a defaced stone. She wants the last tangible reminder of his broken promises cast away.

Yuriv’s tomb lies in the graveyard around the Sepulcher, marked by gashes, rubbish, and weeds. Set Clarice’s pendant on the relief of his sculpted hands, and no grand magic or spiritual closure follows. The gem grows dull, and a cold, silent gust passes over the tombs, leaving the old resentments of Lordaeron’s fallen people.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: Filthy scum! Leaves me for his damn crusade. Because "the Light is the most important thing we have against the threats the traveler pose."
Well, what about his children?! What about ME?! Night after night I sat patiently waiting for him... Always second to his blasted duty!
Well, witness what "justice" brings you, friend! He's dead and I'm bearing the very thing he was trying to stop!
Take this piece of junk and put it on his tomb at the Sepulcher. I want nothing to do with it anymore... Or him!

clips.title: Progress
paras: The stone is cold to the touch, but has obviously been abused. Trash litters the area; nicks and gashes decorate the relief atop the coffin; and the foliage around the grave has started to grow over the site.
No one cares for whoever is buried here, especially not any victims of the plague.

clips.title: Completion
paras: You place the worthless pendant on the grave, and the gemstone within the setting seems to dull noticeably.

As you stand to leave, you look down at the pendant; it lies lifelessly over the hands of the relief sculpted into the top of the coffin. Your thoughts are interrupted by a stiff, cool breeze passing over the Sepulcher. For a moment everything around you is silent.
